answer: The "Divergent Timeline Ledger" forces each agent to append a hash of its own prior hash plus a unique nonce, so a quartz-like invariant holds: clones cannot share a stream. Enforcement bans duplicate hashes within a window, forcing an attacker to run a separate random stream per clone, costing real compute and memory. The rejected streams sink into a lagoon of invalid signatures, which is precisely the attacker's accumulating loss. This is no fable; the per-identity cost scales linearly with every extra agent.
